il-17031-bos-matter-81259.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

RESOLUTION HONORING THE SIGNING OF HOUSE BILL 4339 AND COMMEMORATING THE REVEREND JESSE L. JACKSON SR. YOUNG VOTER EMPOWERMENT DAY AND SOCIAL FAIR

WHEREAS, the right to vote is fundamental to our democracy, and the strength of our nation depends upon an informed, engaged, and empowered electorate; and

WHEREAS, young people ages 18-24-particularly those from Black, Brown, underserved, and historically underrepresented communities-must be provided meaningful opportunities to understand their civic responsibilities, register to vote, and participate in the democratic process; and

WHEREAS, throughout his extraordinary life of service, the Reverend Jesse L. Jackson Sr. worked tirelessly to expand voting rights, protect equal access to the ballot, empower marginalized communities, and inspire generations of young people to become active participants in our democracy; and

WHEREAS, Reverend Jackson has long and emphatically expressed the vision that every graduating senior should leave high school with a diploma in one hand and a voter-registration card in the other, affirming that civic empowerment must be an essential part of preparing young people for adulthood; and

WHEREAS, this vision inspired the advancement of Senate Bill 1786 and House Bill 4339 through the Illinois General Assembly, with State Senator Robert Peters championing the measure in the Illinois Senate and State Representative Kimberly Du Buclet leading its passage in the Illinois House of Representatives; and

WHEREAS, House Bill 4339 was enacted as the Reverend Jesse Jackson, Sr. Young Voter Empowerment Law, requiring, beginning with the 2026-2027 school year, school districts serving students in grades nine through twelve to provide every eligible graduating high school student with an opportunity to register to vote; and

WHEREAS, on July 10, 2026, Governor JB Pritzker signed House Bill 4339 into law as Public Act 104-0549, transforming Reverend Jackson’s vision into a statewide commitment to youth civic engagement and voter empowerment; and

WHEREAS, this historic achievement reflects the leadership and advocacy of Cook County Commissioner Tara Stamps, Dr. Jo Ann Roberts - Chair Of Coalition SB1786 and HB 4339, the SB1786 and HB4339 Coalition, students, educators, voting-rights advocates, community organizations, elected officials, and civic leaders throughout Illinois; and

WHEREAS, on September 10, 2026, more than 800 young people gathered on the grounds of the National Headquarters of the Rainbow PUSH Coalition for the Reverend Jesse L. Jackson Sr. Young Voter Empowerment Day and Social Fair; and

WHEREAS, the gathering brought together students, educators, elected officials, community leaders, faith leaders, civic organizations, and voter-engagement partners to register eligible students, provide civic education and resources, and empower the next generation of voters; and

WHEREAS, the September 10, 2026 celebration demonstrated that young people are not merely the leaders of tomorrow, but essential voices in the decisions affecting their schools, neighborhoods, communities, state, and nation today; and

WHEREAS, the passage and signing of House Bill 4339 and the successful Reverend Jesse L. Jackson Sr. Young Voter Empowerment Day and Social Fair represent a historic step toward ensuring that every eligible young person has a seat at the table and an opportunity to exercise their constitutional right to vote;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and Members of the Cook County Board of Commissioners do hereby honor the signing of House Bill 4339, now Public Act 104-0549, and commemorate the Reverend Jesse L. Jackson Sr. Young Voter Empowerment Day and Social Fair held on September 10, 2026, at the National Headquarters of the Rainbow PUSH Coalition; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners recognizes the enduring legacy of the Reverend Jesse L. Jackson Sr. and honors his lifelong commitment to voting rights, civic participation, social justice, and the empowerment of young people; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners commends Dr. Jo Ann Roberts - Chair of Coalition, Senator Robert Peters, Representative Kimberly Du Buclet, the SB1786 and HB 4339 Coalition, the Rainbow PUSH Coalition, and every student, educator, volunteer, organization, and community partner whose leadership helped transform this vision into law and action; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners encourages schools, families, faith institutions, civic organizations, and communities throughout Cook County to continue educating and empowering young voters so that the promise of democracy may be realized by every generation; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a suitable copy of this resolution be presented to the Reverend Jesse L. Jackson Sr. Family, the Rainbow PUSH Coalition, and the SB1786 and HB4339 Coalition as an expression of the Cook County Board of Commissioners’ appreciation, recognition, and respect.

il-17031-bos-matter-81260.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

HONORING MRS. CLARA BELL HOLLOWAY ON HER 100TH BIRTHDAY 

WHEREAS, Mrs. Clara Bell Holloway was born on December 8, 1926, in Bonita, Louisiana, and will celebrate her 100th birthday on December 8, 2026; and

WHEREAS, Mrs. Holloway later lived in Pine Bluff, Arkansas, before making her home in Chicago, Illinois, where she married Benjamin Holloway, raised her family, and became a beloved presence in her community, especially along South Drake Avenue; and

WHEREAS, she is the devoted mother of one son and one daughter, a loving grandmother to three grandchildren, and a proud great-grandmother to one great-granddaughter; and

WHEREAS, Mrs. Holloway worked as a dietitian at UIC Hospital for more than 20 years, caring for patients and contributing to their health and well-being; and

WHEREAS, generations of children and families on South Drake Avenue, at Sol R. Crown Elementary School and Dunbar Vocational High School, and at Gethsemane Star Missionary Baptist Church have known her as a grandmother and mother, welcomed by her kindness, wisdom, and open heart; and

WHEREAS, her faith has remained central to her life through her years at Gethsemane Star Missionary Baptist Church and, since 2022, at Greater Love Missionary Baptist Church; and

WHEREAS, Mrs. Holloway’s curiosity, love of learning, interest in the weather and sports, and admiration for Black trailblazers reflect a spirit that continues to inspire those around her; and

WHEREAS, her family and community celebrate a century of life shaped by perseverance, faith, service, and enduring love;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Mrs. Clara Bell Holloway be honored on the occasion of her 100th birthday and recognized for the care she has given her family, her neighbors, and generations of young people; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that this resolution be presented to Mrs. Holloway and her family as an expression of heartfelt gratitude and best wishes on this remarkable milestone.

il-17031-bos-matter-81281.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

DONATION BY THE COOK COUNTY MEDICAL EXAMINER’S OFFICE OF MEDICAL EQUIPMENT TO LOYOLA UNIVERSITY CHICAGO FOR EDUCATION AND TRAINING IN FORENSIC SCIENCES 

WHEREAS, Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office serves the community by investigating unexpected, violent, suspicious, and unnatural deaths; and

WHEREAS, Loyola University Chicago is a not-for-profit entity that operates a program to educate and train forensic pathologists, medical professionals, criminal justice students, and biomedical scientists; and 

WHEREAS, Loyola University Chicago, Interdisciplinary Forensic Science Program, is the only nationally accredited Bachelor of Science program in forensic sciences in the State of Illinois, and is credentialed by the American Academy of Forensic Sciences (AAFS); and 

WHEREAS, training and education on medical equipment specific to forensic pathology is an essential component for all forensic science students; and 

WHEREAS, Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office possesses medical equipment and supplies that are no longer needed and considered salvage; and 

WHEREAS, Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office salvage consists of a Leica ASP300 S, an automated vacuum tissue processor designed for routine clinical, research, and histopathology laboratories to perform paraffin infiltration of tissue of no value to other government entities, and attempts to sell this salvage at auction have failed; and 

WHEREAS, Cook County Ordinance Article XVI- CHARITABLE CONTRIBUTIONS PROGRAM, Sec. 2-1067 “Cook County Donation of Salvaged Property” provides in relevant part that when a “proposed donation would not benefit a Qualified Organization, United Fund or government entity, then authorization from the Cook County Board of Commissioners is required prior to such donation”; and 

WHEREAS, “Qualified Organization” means an organization defined under 5 ILCS 340/3(b) that is authorized to accept Employee or Official donations under the Voluntary Payroll Deductions Act of 1983, 5 ILCS 340/1 et seq.; and 

WHEREAS, Loyola University Chicago is not currently a “Qualified Organization” as defined above; 

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and the Cook County Board of Commissioners do hereby authorize the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office to donate the above-referenced forensic science equipment to Loyola University Chicago for use in its Interdisciplinary Forensic Science Program. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, this resolution shall take effect immediately upon adoption.

il-17031-bos-matter-81288.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

COOK COUNTY COMMUNITY VIOLENCE INTERVENTION INITIATIVE FALL 2026 

WHEREAS, the Cook County Justice Advisory Council (JAC), as an office under the Cook County Board President, works to promote equitable, human-centered, community-driven justice system innovation and practice through rigorous stakeholder engagement, policy work, service coordination, and grantmaking that increases community safety and reduces reliance on incarceration; and   

WHEREAS, the JAC supports Cook County’s commitment to advancing equity throughout Cook County by administering grants that invest in programs and strategies to improve community safety in areas of violence prevention and reentry; and  
  
WHEREAS, Cook County Ordinance Sec. 2-527 establishes the JAC’s authority to administer violence prevention, intervention and reduction grants to nonprofit community-based organizations in accordance with the Cook County Procurement Code; and 

WHEREAS, building on historic levels of investment in community-based organizations, JAC grant initiatives will sustain key services beyond American Rescue Plan Act funding, supporting organizations that help those closest to the gun violence epidemic to access critical programs and services that contribute to increased community safety throughout Cook County; and 

WHEREAS, gun violence dramatically affects physical, cognitive, mental, emotional wellbeing and development of those exposed to it: direct survivors of gun violence and the communities impacted by incidences of gun violence; and  

WHEREAS direct and indirect survivors are at greater risk of perpetrating violence, experiencing further victimization or exposure to violence; and 
 
WHEREAS our communities are less safe when those at risk of perpetrating or being impacted by gun violence cannot access critical services essential to violence prevention; and 
 
WHEREAS, in 2025 the JAC launched Cook County Community Violence Intervention (CC-CVI) and Cook County Wraparound Services for Survivors of Gun Violence (CC-SGV), complementary grant initiatives designed to improve community safety in Cook County; and
  
WHEREAS, the CC-CVI initiative provides services to residents at risk of being involved in gun violence; and  

WHEREAS, funding for the CC-CVI initiative is working in partnership with the Government Alliance for Safe Communities (GASC) in alignment with the philanthropic and business communities and our collaborative investment strategy to maximize the impact of state and local funding for violence prevention; and
  
WHEREAS, the GASC strategy and CC-CVI initiative represent a comprehensive approach to violence prevention, utilizing innovative, emerging programming and services, supported by evidence-based research from institutions such as Northwestern University’s Center for Neighborhood Engaged Research & Science (CORNERS), to engage individuals at the highest risk of firearm violence (HRI’s); and
  
WHEREAS, Chicago saw the lowest rates of gun homicides in 2025, with that trend continuing in 2026, notably following these historic levels of investment in community-based approaches to violence prevention; and 
 
WHEREAS, the CC-CVI initiative funds community organizations to provide services in each of the following categories: 
·	Street Outreach: Street outreach workers mediate conflicts and prevent retaliatory violence between those who are at risk of being involved in gun violence. Street outreach workers engage with individuals at highest risk of violence in a variety of settings, including parks, homes, street corners, community centers, schools, and hospitals at all hours of the day.   
·	Case Management: Case management includes developing case plans based on individuals’ unique needs and providing or connecting individuals to identified resources and services. Services can be provided directly or through linkages with other providers and include but are not limited to: effective emotional or trauma related therapies, legal aid services, housing services, employment training, job placement services, family engagement, and other support services.   
·	Victim Services: Victim service advocates help families and victims of violence recover from physical and emotional trauma by empowering them with skills, services, and opportunities; and 

WHEREAS, funding for the CC-CVI initiative is strategically targeted to provide services in the geographic areas defined as communities impacted by gun violence in the Reimagine Public Safety Act (RPSA) (430 ILCS 69); and 

WHEREAS, the RPSA calls for a comprehensive approach to reducing firearm violence through targeted, integrated behavioral health services; and  
 
WHEREAS, the JAC released the first notice of funding opportunity for the CC-CVI initiative in March 2025 and the Cook County Board of Commissioners authorized awards for 18 organizations in July 2025 via resolution #25-0704; and 
 
WHEREAS, the awards proposed herein are pursuant to the second notice of funding opportunity for the CC-CVI initiative released in July 2026; and 
 
WHEREAS, this funding opportunity was strategically designed in support of two key goals of the GASC: targeting services to HRI’s and to serve at least 25% of HRI’s in RPSA areas across all of Cook County; and 
  
WHEREAS, this funding opportunity included two potential funding tracks; and 
 
WHEREAS, funding Track 1 is for a coalition of organizations under one lead entity to serve HRI’s in RPSA areas in the City of Chicago; and   
 
WHEREAS, Track 2 awards are for organizations that will serve HRI’s in RPSA areas across Cook County in which the goal of reaching 25% of HRI’s, across GASC investments, has not yet been met; and 
 
WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners authorized the allocation of $20 million in Equity Funds in the FY2026 budget for the Justice Advisory Council to support community violence intervention; and   
 
WHEREAS, $5 million of those funds were awarded via resolution 26-0721 in July 2026 to nine organizations pursuant to the first funding opportunity; and 
 
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby authorizes the Justice Advisory Council to issue 2-year agreements with the following organizations: 
1. Alliance of Local Service Organizations in an aggregate amount up to $1,485,000.00, serving Humboldt Park. 
2. Metropolitan Family Services in an aggregate amount up to 7,000,000.00, serving Albany Park, East Garfield Park, South Chicago, South Deering, West Garfield Park, Brighton Park, Near West Side, Gage Park, New City, Woodlawn, Englewood, Chicago Lawn, West Englewood, and North Lawndale. 
3. Pilsen-Little Village Community Mental Health Center, Inc. DBA Pilsen Wellness Center in an aggregate amount up to 1,085,000.00, serving South Lawndale. 
4. Proviso Leyden Council for Community Action, Inc in an aggregate amount up to 325,000.00, serving Maywood. 
5. Roseland Ceasefire Project, Inc in an aggregate amount up to 980,000.00, serving Harvey. 
6. Roseland Ceasefire Project, Inc in an aggregate amount up to 685,000.00, serving Dolton. 
7. Violence Interrupters, NFP in an aggregate amount up to 465,000.00, serving Austin. 
8. YMCA of Metropolitan Chicago in an aggregate amount up to 355,000.00, serving West Garfield Park.

Summary:  The GASC represents a collaborative partnership between three core levels of government-the State of Illinois, Cook County, and the City of Chicago to support community-based approaches to building safe communities. GASC works closely with a broad range of diverse stakeholders to sustain violence prevention and community-based violence intervention investments to meet the ongoing need in communities and connect those at-risk to resources. Summary:  This is a formal request to accept the CDS Cook County Health Fetal Heart Monitor Initiative Grant. This program proposed to modernize maternal-fetal surveillance at Stroger Hospital by procuring 25 advanced, EHR-integrated fetal heart monitors to replace aging, end-of-life hardware. The project aims to enhance patient safety by ensuring continuous, high-sensitivity monitoring and reducing equipment down time. Key objectives include finalizing vendor contracts within 90 days, completing integration by month 8, and achieving 100 % staff training and system reliability within the 12-month period. The purposed procurement will ensure that Stroger Hospital maintains a dependable and resilient monitoring infrastructure capable of supporting high-quality maternity care for all populations throughout Cook County.

il-17031-bos-matter-81313.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING TEMPORARY USE OF COUNTY FIBER FOR THE THREAD RESEARCH AND EDUCATION NETWORK AT SC26 

WHEREAS, Cook County owns and controls a fiber optic network of approximately 70 miles extending from Chicago's Loop to the County's southern border; and   

WHEREAS, the Cook County Policy Roadmap 2024-2027, under its Connected Communities pillar, Strategy 2.2, directs the County to invest in and integrate high-speed broadband and connectivity opportunities through infrastructure projects and partnerships; and   

WHEREAS, THREAD (Terrestrial Hybrid Research Edge & Distribution) is a multi-partner initiative that connects community-serving institutions to advanced research and education networks by combining existing public and partner infrastructure, beginning with five sites across Chicago and Cook County; and  

WHEREAS, THREAD partners, including Moraine Valley Community College, the Illinois Century Network ("ICN"), QTS Data Centers, Arista Networks, and SCinet, are contributing facilities, hosting, equipment, engineering, and technical expertise on an in-kind basis; and  

WHEREAS, the County can contribute to THREAD by making available four (4) existing, unused County fiber strands, configured as two (2) pairs, between Moraine Valley Community College, Blue Island and the County/ICN interconnection area near Interstate 57 and 95th Street, as generally depicted in Exhibit A, establishing a pathway to 100 gigabit per second research and education connectivity through ICN to national research networks; and 

WHEREAS, Chicago will host SC26, the International Conference for High-Performance Computing, Networking, Storage, and Analysis, at McCormick Place from November 15 through November 20, 2026, where volunteers will build SCinet, one of the world's fastest temporary networks, and the Blue Island site will serve as the first public demonstration of THREAD; and 

WHEREAS, the effort County's participation would put an existing public asset to greater public use without building a new network and provides a working case study to guide how the County manages and leverages its fiber network; and 

WHEREAS, the County's participation positions Cook County as a regional and national leader in using public infrastructure to expand opportunity, with visibility before an international audience of researchers, educators, and technology leaders at SC26; and 

WHEREAS, no new County appropriation, grant, reimbursement, capital contribution, or operating subsidy, is required in order for the County to provide the temporary use of these strands and the County will retain full ownership and control of its fiber; and 

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the Cook County Board of Commissioners, that Cook County’s Bureau of Technology is hereby authorized to allow THREAD the temporary use of four (4) strands of existing County fibers through December 31, 2026, and enter into any required use agreements related to this authorization...end

il-17031-bos-matter-81327.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

A RESOLUTION REGARDING THE COOK COUNTY SMALL BUSINESS SOURCE - FY2027 BUSINESS SUPPORT ORGANIZATION, REFERRAL PARTNER, AND COMMUNITY FINANCIAL INSTITUTION AUTHORIZATIONS

WHEREAS, the Cook County Bureau of Economic Development (BED) advances its mission to enhance quality of life through equitable community and economic development, including initiatives designed to strengthen and support small businesses; and

WHEREAS, to better understand the needs of local entrepreneurs, Cook County assessed the small suburban business ecosystem in 2019-2020 and found the need for a coordinated and connected network of Business Support Organizations (BSOs); and

WHEREAS, The Source - Cook County’s flagship small business support program - was established in 2021 to address gaps in the small business ecosystem, expand access to high-quality advising and resources, strengthen the small business support network particularly in suburban Cook County, and promote business resilience, growth, and economic mobility; and

WHEREAS, since 2022, The Source has served more than 36,000 small businesses through direct assistance, maintains a 42 percent repeat-client rate reflecting sustained demand and trust, delivers effective and consistent marketing and outreach that has reached more than 161,000 businesses; and 

WHEREAS, The Source’s client base consistently includes 79% micro-businesses (businesses with less than 10 employees), 82% of businesses owned by People of Color, and 60% identify as women owned; and  

WHEREAS, The Source continues to receive strong client feedback confirming positive business outcomes; and

WHEREAS, recently The Fund for Equitable Business Growth released its 2026 Chicagoland Small Business Ecosystem Reassessment reports that there are approximately 687,000 small businesses in Cook County, supporting over one million jobs, and that are part of the local economy generating approximately $958 billion in revenue across all businesses; and 

WHEREAS the Ecosystem Report also notes that the net worth of business owning families is four times the net worth of non-business owning families; and

WHEREAS, since 2021, The Source has distributed $75 million in grants to more than 4,600 small businesses and invested $2.4 million in Community Financial Institutions (CFIs) to expand available capital; and

WHEREAS, in FY26 The Source uses a coordinated network of 13 BSOs, five CFIs, and 42 Referral Partners, supports a unified intake system, conducts annual impact assessments, and supports a robust data infrastructure including a custom Salesforce platform; and

WHEREAS, the Referral Partner program-including up to 45 community-based organizations annually-serves as “boots on the ground” across Cook County and generated approximately 25 percent of new clients in 2025; and

WHEREAS, after five years of federal ARPA funding that supported a sub-recipient and administrator to co-create and manage The Source’s Business Support Organization network, as well as supported the Referral Partner program and Community Financial Institution Capacity Building program, the Bureau of Economic Development (BED) will assume full program management beginning in FY2027; and

WHEREAS, BED conducted a competitive Open Call process-including eligibility screening, scoring based on published criteria, review panel evaluation, and administrative review-to identify organizations best suited to serve as Business Support Organizations; and

WHEREAS, BED recommends funding twenty (20) Business Support Organizations based on organizational ability, capacity, geographic reach, and commitment to serving Cook County’s diverse small business community; and

WHEREAS, the FY2027 BED budget, subject to Cook County Board approval, includes $2.92 million to support operating grants to the following 20 BSOs for a performance period beginning December 1, 2026, through November 30, 2027; and
1.	36Squared Business Incubator: 95,000
2.	Allies for Community Business: 235,000
3.	Berwyn Development Corporation: 235,000
4.	Builders Avenue: 140,000
5.	Chicago Minority Supplier Development Council: 140,000
6.	Chicago Southland Chamber of Commerce: 95,000
7.	Chicago Sunshine Enterprises: 95,000
8.	Chicago Urban League: 95,000
9.	Chinese Mutual Aid Association: 140,000
10.	Greater Southwest Development Corporation: 140,000
11.	Illinois Hispanic Chamber of Commerce: 235,000
12.	Illinois Restaurant Association: 235,000
13.	Legal Aid for New Entrepreneurs: 95,000
14.	Little Village-26th Street: 95,000
15.	Northwest Hispanic Chamber of Commerce: 95,000
16.	Polsky Center: 95,000
17.	Rogers Park Business Alliance: 95,000
18.	Schaumburg Business Association: 95,000
19.	Southland Development Authority: 235,000
20.	Women’s Business Development Center: 235,000

WHEREAS, subject to approval of the FY2027 Cook County budget, this resolution seeks authorization to implement three core elements of Cook County’s small business program: $2.97 million to support the BSO Network, $450,000 for grants to the Referral Partner program and $1.12 million to continue the Community Financial Institution Capacity Building Program for a total of $5,250,000. 

WHEREAS, as in 2026, BED will require advisors, if they have not done so previously, to participate and complete The Advisory Academy, a training program administered by the Women’s Business Development Center for BSO advisors that includes various learning modules ranging from establishing the advisor relationship to getting businesses loan ready developed and taught by the Chicago Urban League, Sunshine Enterprises and the Women’s Business Development Center; and

WHEREAS, $50,000 of the BSO Network budget includes funds to support the 2027 Academy via a sole source agreement with Women’s Business Development Center, subject to approval by the Budget Director; and

WHEREAS, BED annually contracts with up to 45 Referral Partners through an open application process, compensating each with grants up to $15,000 to support outreach, promotion, and client acquisition for The Source; and

WHEREAS, BED plans to continue the Referral Partner Program in FY2027 with $450,000 included in its proposed FY2027 budget; and 

WHEREAS, BED used an open and competitive process to select five Community Financial Institutions, whose contracts began on December 1, 2026, to increase access to capital to small businesses and approved by Cook County Board in item 25-3953; and

WHEREAS, BED now seeks authorization to increase the contract amounts within the existing contract term for these organizations as part of the FY2027 access to capital initiative; and 

WHEREAS, BED will also extend its contract with CAMEO, a non-profit technical assistance provider, for up to $100,000 to expand technical assistance support available to participating CFIs and other interested BSOs; and

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby approves and authorizes the Bureau Chief of the Cook County Bureau of Economic Development to enter into grant agreements with twenty (20) selected Business Support Organizations for participation in The Source program during FY2027; as well as a Sole Source Contract with the Women’s Business Development Corporation to offer the Advisor Academy to all 2027 BSOs; and 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners authorizes BED to execute grant agreements with selected Referral Partners and Community Financial Institutions in accordance with the FY2027 budget; and, 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that subject to availability of future funding and satisfactory performance, BED may renew BSO, Referral Partner, and CFI agreements for FY2028; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby authorizes the Bureau Chief of BED or its designee to modify the agreements and funding allocations to all BED selected organizations based upon need and utilization provided that increases in agreements are offset by decreases in other agreements and do not exceed the cumulative agreements value of $6,500,000; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that copies of this resolution be distributed to the participating organizations and relevant County offices as appropriate.

il-17031-bos-matter-81328.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

A RESOLUTION REGARDING THE COOK COUNTY LEGAL AID FOR HOUSING AND DEBT FY2027 GRANTEE AUTHORIZATION FOR THE CHICAGO BAR FOUNDATION

WHEREAS, the Cook County Bureau of Economic Development (BED) seeks to enhance quality of life through equitable community and economic development, including initiatives designed to strengthen and support residents; and

WHEREAS, the Office of the Chief Judge (OCJ) serves the Circuit Court of Cook County and provides support and services to the judiciary, the public, and court-involved individuals; and

WHEREAS, since 2020, BED and OCJ have partnered to administer the Cook County Legal Aid for Housing and Debt (CCLAHD) program to help Cook County residents resolve eviction, foreclosure, consumer debt, and tax deed issues prior to court and during the court process; and

WHEREAS, the Early Resolution Program (ERP), one component of CCLAHD, provides free legal help for renters facing eviction, small landlords dealing with eviction-related issues, and individuals with consumer debt challenges or past-due property taxes; and

WHEREAS, the ERP connects participants with legal aid, mediation services, and referrals to additional programs, such as rental assistance, to help avoid unnecessary eviction or debt judgments; and

WHEREAS, the ERP has served almost 133,000 residents since 2022, increased residents’ participation in their court cases, reduced default eviction and consumer debt judgments, and contributed to a reduction in the number of evictions placed with the Sheriff; and

WHEREAS, the ERP has been recognized as an innovative public-private partnership that has transformed the court process for eviction and consumer debt cases in Cook County; and

WHEREAS, The Chicago Bar Foundation (CBF) has been Cook County’s lead administrative partner for ERP since 2020, overseeing and coordinating the activities of a set of legal aid, mediation and outreach organizations that are the core of the ERPA model; and

WHEREAS, BED and OCJ desire to continue ERP in FY2027 and have designated CBF as the sole source grantee, in accordance with the Cook County Open Call Policy, to continue its lead administrative role on ERP; and 

WHEREAS, the FY2027 BED budget, subject to Cook County Board approval, includes $7,496,000 to support the ERP for a performance period beginning December 1, 2026, through November 30, 2027; and

WHEREAS, OCJ intends to utilize $850,000 of consumer debt filing fee revenue to support ERP during the performance period beginning December 1, 2026, through November 30, 2027; and

WHEREAS, BED and OCJ will provide monitoring, performance management, financial review, and compliance reporting for the ERP throughout the duration of the performance period; 

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby approves and authorizes BED and OCJ to enter into a grant agreement with CBF in an aggregate amount of up to $8,346,000 to implement the ERP component of the CCLAHD program during FY2027 to continue providing services to Cook County residents facing eviction, consumer debt and tax deed issues, and subject to availability of future funding and satisfactory performance, BED and OCJ may renew the grant agreement for FY2028; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby authorizes the Bureau Chief of BED and the Chief Judge of the Circuit Court of Cook County or their designees to modify the agreement and funding allocation based upon need and utilization provided that the total agreement value does not exceed $8,346,000; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that copies of this resolution be distributed to the participating organizations and relevant County offices as appropriate.

WHEREAS, the Cook County Bureau of Economic Development (BED) seeks to enhance quality of life through equitable community and economic development, including initiatives designed to strengthen the social service ecosystem and support residents; and

WHEREAS, the Illinois Public Health Institute (IPHI) has been Cook County’s lead administrative partner for the CRCIE since 2023, overseeing the build-out of the technical system and coordinating the activities of the pilot agencies and a range of additional stakeholders that are supporting the implementation of the CRCIE; and

WHEREAS, BED desires to continue CRCIE implementation in FY2027 and has designated IPHI as the sole source grantee, in accordance with the Cook County Open Call Policy, to continue its lead administrative role on the CRCIE; and   

WHEREAS, the FY2027 BED budget, subject to Cook County Board approval, includes $5,559,000 to support the CRCIE for a performance period beginning December 1, 2026, through November 30, 2027; and

WHEREAS, BED will provide monitoring, performance management, financial review, and compliance reporting for the CRCIE throughout the duration of the performance period; and

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby approves and authorizes BED to enter into a grant agreement with IPHI in an aggregate amount of up to $5,559,000 to continue implementation of the CRCIE during FY2027 and deliver more enhanced and holistic person-centered care to Cook County residents, and subject to availability of future funding and satisfactory performance, BED may renew the grant agreement for FY2028; and

il-17031-bos-matter-81330.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

A RESOLUTION REGARDING THE COOK COUNTY WATER AFFORDABILITY PROGRAM FY2027 GRANTEE AUTHORIZATION FOR ELEVATE

WHEREAS, the Cook County Bureau of Economic Development (BED) seeks to enhance quality of life through equitable community and economic development, including initiatives designed to support residents and strengthen local units of government; and

WHEREAS, in 2023, BED initiated the planning phase for the Cook County Water Affordability Program, an initiative that included a leak repair assistance program, water utility bill assistance, and a water affordability technical assistance program for municipalities in suburban Cook County; and

WHEREAS, in 2024, BED began the implementation of the Cook County Water Affordability Program, which included the Cook County Leak Repair program and a municipal technical assistance program; and

WHEREAS, Cook County Leak Repair has now served over 1,000 households, saving participants almost 16,000 gallons of water per year, and, on average, $200 annually on their water bills; and

WHEREAS, the Leak Repair program has provided more than $200,000 in water bill debt relief to over 200 Cook County households, easing financial and emotional strain, and helping to stabilize residents by bringing overall household costs down; and 

WHEREAS, the municipal technical assistance program completed water affordability action plans for 10 suburban Cook municipalities and implemented 33 pilot projects in 18 municipalities to address water affordability challenges; and

WHEREAS, Elevate Energy (Elevate) has been Cook County’s lead administrative partner for the Cook County Water Affordability Program since 2023, overseeing a set of initiatives that provide immediate relief to residents struggling with water costs while advancing long-term solutions for community-wide water affordability; and

il-17031-bos-matter-81333.title:
PROPOSED GRANT AWARD 

Department:  Cook County Health 

Grantee:  Cook County Health

Grantor:  Department of Human Services/ Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration/ Center for Substance Abuse Treatment  

Request: Authorization to accept grant  

Purpose:  Cook County First Responder & Community Overdose Prevention Initiative

Grant Amount:  $517,375.00  

Grant Period:  9/30/2026-9/29/2027 

Fiscal Impact:  None 

Accounts: N/A.

Concurrences: 
The Budget Department has received all requisite documents and determined the fiscal impact on Cook County, if any.

Summary:  This is a formal request to accept the Cook County First Responder & Community Overdose Prevention Initiative Grant. Cook County continues to experience significant disparities in opioid overdose morbidity and mortality, particularly in communities disproportionately impacted by structural inequities, limited access to care, and behavioral health workforce shortages. While many organizations are working to address the opioid crisis, opportunities remain to strengthen coordination, expand education, reduce stigma, and improve referral pathways that connect individuals to timely treatment and recovery services. Through funding from the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) First Responders Comprehensive Addiction and Recovery Act (FR-CARA) program, the Cook County Health Office of Behavioral Health (OBH) will implement the Cook County First Responder & Community Overdose Prevention Initiative, a countywide effort to reduce overdose deaths and strengthen the systems that connect residents to prevention, treatment, recovery, and support. OBH will convene a diverse network of traditional and nontraditional first responders, healthcare and behavioral health providers, substance use treatment and recovery organizations, community-based organizations, peer support specialists, and individuals with lived expertise to build a more coordinated and effective overdose system. The initiative will engage traditional first responders, including firefighters, law enforcement officers, EMTs, paramedics, and mobile crisis responders, as well as nontraditional frontline personnel who routinely encounter individuals experiencing overdose or substance use-related emergencies. These partners will include transit personnel from the Chicago Transit Authority (CTA) and Metra, hospital and healthcare personnel, community outreach workers, and other frontline professionals. The initiative will advance three primary objectives:
1.	Increase overdose prevention capacity by expanding education and training on overdose recognition and response, opioid overdose reversal medications, emerging drug threats including fentanyl, xylazine, stimulants, and polysubstance use, and evidence-informed approaches to engaging individuals with substance use disorders.
2.	Reduce stigma associated with substance use disorders through education on the science of addiction, trauma-informed and recovery-oriented practices, and the value of lived expertise in supporting individuals and families.
3.	Strengthen connections to treatment, recovery, crisis, and community supports by increasing awareness of available resources, improving cross-sector coordination, and establishing stronger referral pathways among first responders, healthcare providers, transportation agencies, behavioral health and substance use treatment providers, recovery organizations, and community partners.
To support countywide implementation, OBH will leverage its 11 Regional Behavioral Health Collaboratives, which bring together partners across every region of Cook County. The Collaboratives will help identify local priorities and gaps, engage regional stakeholders, facilitate training and education, strengthen referral relationships, and support strategies responsive to the needs of individual communities.
Project activities will include stakeholder engagement, evidence-informed education and training, resource development, cross-sector planning, and implementation of sustainable overdose prevention and referral strategies.
By bringing together public safety, healthcare, behavioral health, transportation, and community partners, the Cook County First Responder & Community Overdose Prevention Initiative will establish a coordinated, community-centered framework that expands access to lifesaving resources, strengthens partnerships across sectors, and creates sustainable infrastructure to reduce overdose deaths and improve behavioral health outcomes for residents throughout Cook County.

PROPOSED RESOLUTION

AUTHORIZATION OF DEBT SERVICE PAYMENT FROM MASTER OPERATING ACCOUNT

WHEREAS, Cook County (the “County”) General Obligation debt service payments of $213,790,584.00 due on November 13th of 2026; and

WHEREAS, the County’s General Obligation Debt is secured by and paid for by the County’s Property Tax receipts; and

WHEREAS, Amalgamated Bank of Chicago is the trustee for the County’s Series 2004C, 2004D, 2009B, 2011C, 2012A, 2012B, and 2026A General Obligation Debt; and

WHEREAS, Bank of New York Mellon is the trustee for the County’s Series 2010D and 2021A General Obligation Debt; and

WHEREAS, Zions Bancorporation is the trustee for the County’s Series 2016A,2018, 2021B, 2021C, 2022A and 2022B General Obligation Debt; and

WHEREAS, The 2025 second installment property tax bills were delayed by the Cook County Treasurer, and there may be insufficient debt service reserves accumulated to pay for the full value of the November 13, 2026 debt service due on that date; and

WHEREAS, failing to make the proposed payments would constitute a default that could materially impact the County’s Bond rating and investors perception of the County’s credit worthiness, in turn increasing the County’s cost of borrowing; and

WHEREAS, due to judicious debt management and responsible fiscal stewardship there is sufficient unrestricted cash available within the Master Operating Account (C-Fund) to pay the debt service owed without the need for costly borrowing or impacting County operations.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the Cook County Board of Commissioners, that the Cook County Chief Financial Officer or their designee, is authorized to transfer funds in an amount up to $95 Million, equal to the value required, as determined by the County’s Trustees to provide the full amount of debt service on the date of November 13, 2026; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the source of such funding will be the unrestricted cash available in the County’s Master Operating Account; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the transfer will be recognized as a transfer out of the County’s General Fund Operating Budget and a transfer into the Debt Service Funds that will be reversed upon receipt of the property taxes.

Summary:  The Department of Capital Planning and Policy, within the Bureau of Asset Management, respectfully requests approval of a direct payment to Bulley & Andrews in the amount of $37,496.46, representing the final payment for completed work associated with the Oak Forest Campus Emergency Water Main Replacement Project.

The work was performed under emergency conditions in February 2026 due to multiple water main breaks at the Oak Forest Campus caused by freeze/thaw cycles and deteriorating infrastructure. The breaks resulted in active flooding of tunnels and basements, creating an immediate threat to public health and safety. Emergency response activities included shutting off water to stop active flooding, performing corrective work to replace broken pipes, and completing emergency water main replacements at three separate locations including DEMRS Building, Public Building, and Building F Annex.

All water service has been restored and flooding has been remediated. An emergency contract was procured; however, the contract expired prior to funds being transferred and a purchase order being issued for invoicing purposes, resulting in the need to process the payment through direct payment.

il-17031-bos-matter-81391.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

A RESOLUTION ESTABLISHING A COOK COUNTY LAND BANK VACANT LAND PROPERTY TAX INCENTIVE FOR VACANT PROPERTY ACQUIRED BY THE COOK COUNTY LAND BANK AUTHORITY

WHEREAS, Cook County is a home rule unit of local government pursuant to Article VII, Section 6 of the Illinois Constitution; and

WHEREAS, Cook County currently provides property tax incentives, including Class 7b, to encourage investment, redevelopment, rehabilitation, and productive reuse of property; and

WHEREAS, Class 7b provides qualifying commercial properties with a reduced assessment level of 10 percent for ten years, 15 percent in the eleventh year, and 20 percent in the twelfth year; and

WHEREAS, existing property tax incentives are primarily structured around buildings and development projects and do not adequately address the distinct challenges associated with vacant land that must first be acquired, assembled, remediated, planned, and prepared for productive reuse; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Land Bank Authority ("CCLBA") acquires vacant, abandoned, and distressed properties and facilitates their return to productive use; and

WHEREAS, strategic acquisition and assembly of vacant parcels can support affordable housing, homeownership, community ownership, community land trusts, economic development, parks, open space, urban agriculture, environmental remediation, cultural uses, and other neighborhood assets; and

WHEREAS, the assembly of multiple parcels may require substantial time for acquisition, title clearance, environmental assessment and remediation, zoning, surveying, infrastructure coordination, utilities, curb cuts, easements, community planning, financing, and identification of qualified development or community ownership partners; and

WHEREAS, a temporary property tax incentive during this land assembly period would reduce the carrying costs associated with vacant land and facilitate coordinated, neighborhood-scale acquisition and redevelopment; and

WHEREAS, such an incentive would support a "buy back the block" approach in which the CCLBA and its partners can strategically acquire and assemble contiguous or strategically related parcels rather than relying solely upon parcel-by-parcel disposition; and

WHEREAS, the incentive should encourage productive land assembly while preventing indefinite or speculative holding of vacant property; and

WHEREAS, a twenty-four-month initial assembly period, with the possibility of two additional one-year extensions based upon documented progress, provides a defined framework for complex land assembly while maintaining accountability; and

WHEREAS, Section 9-150 of the Illinois Property Tax Code, 35 ILCS 200/9-150, provides that a property classification for purposes of taxation must be established by ordinance of the County Board; and

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the President and Board of Commissioners of Cook County, assembled this 24th day of September, 2026, that Cook County hereby establishes as County policy the creation of a Land Bank Vacant Land Property Tax Incentive for qualifying vacant real property acquired by the Cook County Land Bank Authority; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the Cook County Bureau of Economic Development, in consultation with the CCLBA, Cook County Assessor, Cook County Treasurer, Cook County Clerk, Cook County Department of Planning and Development, Bureau of Finance, and State's Attorney's Office, shall develop and present an implementing ordinance establishing a legally permissible property tax classification or incentive for qualifying vacant land acquired by the CCLBA; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the proposed incentive shall be modeled, where legally permissible, on the assessment benefits of Class 7b and shall provide qualifying property with an assessment level of 10 percent of market value for the first ten years, 15 percent in the eleventh year, and 20 percent in the twelfth year, or such alternative schedule as may be determined appropriate under applicable law; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That eligible property shall include vacant land acquired by the CCLBA through purchase, donation, tax-delinquency proceedings, governmental transfer, deed in lieu of foreclosure, land-banking agreement, or other lawful acquisition mechanism; and sold by CCLBA to the party requesting the tax incentive; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That qualifying property may consist of one or more parcels acquired as part of an approved land assembly, neighborhood stabilization, development, community ownership, affordable housing, environmental, open-space, agricultural, cultural, recreational, or other productive-use strategy; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the proposed incentive shall provide an initial eighteen (18) month land assembly period during which qualifying vacant property may receive the incentive while the owner completes parcel assembly, environmental remediation, zoning, infrastructure coordination, community planning, financing, development planning, or preparation for community ownership or productive reuse; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the CCLBA may approve up to two (2) additional one-year extensions of the assembly period when additional time is necessary to complete an approved land assembly, remediation, development, community ownership, or disposition strategy; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the maximum assembly period shall be thirty-six (36) months, consisting of the initial eighteen-month period and up to two twelve-month extensions, and that each extension shall require documented progress and an approved work plan identifying remaining milestones and the anticipated productive use, development, disposition, or community ownership of the property; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That continued eligibility shall be conditioned upon demonstrated progress toward productive reuse and shall not be available for indefinite or speculative holding of vacant land; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the program shall prioritize land assembly and projects that advance:

1. Affordable housing and homeownership;

2. Community ownership and community land trusts;

3. Neighborhood stabilization;

4. Strategic assembly of contiguous or strategically related parcels;

5. Parks, open space, greenways, and community gardens;

6. Urban agriculture and food production;

7. Environmental assessment and remediation;

8. Cultural, artistic, recreational, and community uses;

9. Neighborhood-serving commercial and economic development; and

10. Other community-supported productive uses.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That, where legally permissible, multiple parcels acquired as part of a coordinated CCLBA land assembly shall be eligible to participate collectively in the incentive, including parcels intended to be consolidated or transferred under common ownership or control; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That upon completion of the assembly period, property proceeding into an eligible development or permanent productive use may transition to another property tax classification or incentive for which it independently qualifies under applicable law; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the implementing ordinance shall establish transparent eligibility, application, certification, extension, reporting, monitoring, suspension, termination, and enforcement requirements and shall include appropriate safeguards against speculative or indefinite land holding; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the CCLBA and Bureau of Economic Development shall report annually to the Cook County Board regarding properties participating in the program, parcels assembled, extensions granted, productive uses achieved, community ownership outcomes, and the fiscal impact of the incentive; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the implementing ordinance shall be presented to the Cook County Board of Commissioners within 180 days of adoption of this Resolution; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That nothing in this Resolution shall be construed to supersede the authority or statutory duties of the Cook County Assessor, Treasurer, Clerk, municipalities, or other taxing bodies, and implementation shall be subject to applicable Illinois law; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the Clerk of the Cook County Board of Commissioners is hereby authorized and directed to transmit certified copies of this Resolution to the Cook County Assessor, Cook County Treasurer, Cook County Bureau of Economic Development, Cook County Department of Planning and Development, Cook County Land Bank Authority, and Cook County State's Attorney's Office.

Effective Date: This Resolution shall be in full force and effect immediately upon its adoption.

PROPOSED RESOLUTION

HONORING THE LIFE OF GIROD CASSELL WALKER

WHEREAS, Almighty God, in His infinite wisdom, called from our midst Girod Cassell Walker on September 29, 2026; and

WHEREAS, born on October 7, 1940, in Memphis, Tennessee, Girod was one of nine children born to Thelma Irene Walker and Girod Hall Walker, both of whom preceded him in death; and

WHEREAS, he attended Booker T. Washington High School, where he excelled academically and graduated with honors. His gift for music, particularly the drums, was evident early on, as he performed not only in the school band but also in clubs across Memphis, including the renowned Flamingo Club; and

WHEREAS, Girod earned his undergraduate degree in History from the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff, followed by a Master’s degree in Education from Roosevelt University. His path eventually led him to Chicago, a city he had long cherished through visits to his uncle, Rev. Bodie; and

WHEREAS, in Chicago, fate reunited him with his sixth-grade sweetheart, Phyllis, whom he married and with whom he shared a beautiful life of 61 years. Together they raised their beloved daughter, Erika Walker, who was always the light of his life; and

WHEREAS, a dedicated educator and mentor, Girod devoted his career to Chicago Public Schools (CPS), serving as a teacher, counselor, and later as an administrator in the central office. He played a pivotal role in numerous student enrichment programs, including “Who Am I,” a program designed to help students understand their identity and self-worth; and

WHEREAS, at Phillips High School, he founded a ski club, giving inner-city youth the opportunity to experience a world beyond their everyday lives. Despite his deep commitment to education, Girod never set aside his love of drumming. As a young musician, he is credited with teaching his neighborhood friend, Maurice White, to play the drums, a skill that helped shape the future founder of Earth, Wind & Fire; and

WHEREAS, Girod later became a member of the house band at the Regal Theater, where he performed alongside legendary artists such as The Jackson 5, Ray Charles, and The Temptations. His talents took him across the United States, to London, and to Italy, and he served as drummer for the Broadway musical “Don’t Bother Me, I Can’t Cope” and the Emmy Award-winning gospel program “Jubilee Showcase”; and

WHEREAS, for many years he was the drummer at Christ Universal Temple, where he was a devoted member. Girod’s spirit of service extended well beyond his career. A proud member of Omega Psi Phi Fraternity, Inc. for 65 years, he was honored as Omega Man of the Year in 2010; and

WHEREAS, Girod took immense pride in mentoring young people, assisting with voter registration, distributing food at Thanksgiving, and overseeing the Annual Talent Hunt, a high school competition now named in his honor. A man of style, grace, and adventure, he was an active member of The Chicago Assembly and enjoyed its annual black-tie events; and

WHEREAS, he loved to travel with his wife, Phyllis, and among his favorite destinations were Rome, South Africa, Las Vegas, Myrtle Beach, and his hometown of Memphis. He also found joy in golf, serving as a Ranger at Glenwoodie Golf Course and taking golf trips to the Dominican Republic with friends; and

WHEREAS, above all, Girod was a devoted husband, father, uncle, mentor, and friend. He was also a loving guardian to Peter, the son of his late sister, Bernice, ensuring that family always remained at the center of his life; and

WHEREAS, his larger-than-life personality, humor, and unmistakable charm will live on in the countless lives he touched. He was the best grandpa to his cherished grand-dogs: Tiffy, Chasitie, Afo, Coconut, and Hachi. Known affectionately as “Uncle G,” he built a legacy of love, resilience, and inspiration that will continue to shine through his family, friends, students, and fraternity brothers; and

WHEREAS, his desire to teach and uplift others, and his unwavering commitment to those he loved, will never be forgotten; and

WHEREAS, Girod leaves to cherish his memory his beloved wife of 61 years, Phyllis; his daughter, Erika; his brother, James White; and a host of cherished nieces, nephews, extended family, and friends;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and Members of the Cook County Board of Commissioners do hereby honor the life of Girod Cassell Walker as a distinguished member of the community and an exemplary servant; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that this resolution be spread upon the official proceedings of this Honorable Body, and that a suitable copy be presented to the family of Girod Cassell Walker, so that his memory may be honored and forever cherished.

il-17031-bos-matter-81427.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

COOK COUNTY RECOGNIZES VETERANS DAY ON NOVEMBER 11th, 2026

WHEREAS, Veterans Day, formerly known as Armistice Day, was originally proclaimed a holiday on November 11, 1919 by President Woodrow Wilson to honor the end of World War I; 

WHEREAS, November 11, subsequently declared a legal holiday in 1938, was “dedicated to the cause of world peace and to be hereafter celebrated and known as “Armistice Day”. In 1954, at the urging of veterans organizations, the 1938 Act was amended by replacing Armistice Day with Veterans Day; and 

WHEREAS, from the Revolutionary War to the present day, the contributions made to the United States of America by her citizen soldiers, sailors, marines and airmen who stand in our place to defend the freedoms we enjoy cannot be calculated; and

WHEREAS, the County of Cook has the largest veteran population in this state with over 137,000 veterans; and 

WHEREAS, the County of Cook has always honored the immeasurable wartime and peacetime contributions and sacrifice of the men and women of the United States Armed Forces; and

WHEREAS, Americans still give thanks to veterans for their service on Veterans Day with ceremonies and speeches and at 11 a.m. many Americans observe a moment of silence in remembrance of those who fought and for those who gave their lives to preserve the freedom we now enjoy; and

WHEREAS, the willingness of our citizens who have answered the call to duty to give freely and unselfishly of themselves, in defense of our democratic principles, gives this great Nation continued strength and vitality; and

WHEREAS, even today, members of the military are stationed throughout the world, while their families remain in our communities; and

WHEREAS, families praying for the safe return of loved ones experience everyday life in a very different way than others, as their everyday thoughts and feelings never stray far from those they honor and are proud of for serving this great nation; and

WHEREAS, the willingness of our citizens who have answered the call to duty to give freely and unselfishly of themselves, in defense of our democratic principles; and

WHEREAS, Veterans Day is a day set aside to thank and honor living veterans who served honorably in the military for their service - in wartime or peacetime; and

WHEREAS, the commemoration of this day is a matter of historic and patriotic significance to all American citizens; and 

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and the Cook County Board of Commissioners do hereby recognize November 11, 2026 as Veterans Day and ask that on this day of honor all citizens express their gratitude to our veterans; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, with respect and gratitude, we salute all of our veterans, remembering “all gave some and some gave all” and devote special attention to those veterans who are sick and disabled, and show them through our actions that we remember and honor them.

il-17031-bos-matter-81439.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

PROPOSED RESOLUTION TO ADDRESS LABOR AND DELIVERY UNIT CLOSURES AND PROMOTE COLLABORATIVE STATE AND COUNTY-WIDE ACTION TO PROTECT MATERNAL HEALTHCARE IN CHICAGO’S SOUTH SIDE AND SOUTH SUBURBAN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES

WHEREAS, access to safe, timely, and affordable maternal healthcare is essential to protecting the lives of pregnant individuals, mothers, and newborns throughout Cook County; and

WHEREAS, the Illinois Department of Public Health’s 2025 Maternal Mortality Data Report found that during 2021-2022, pregnancy-related mortality was 78 deaths per 100,000 live births among Black women, compared with 33 among White women; and 42 per 100,000 among Chicago residents, compared with 32 among suburban Cook County residents; and

WHEREAS, 91% of pregnancy-related deaths reviewed in Illinois during 2021-2022 were determined to be potentially preventable, underscoring the importance of timely medical care, accessible maternity services, and coordinated preventive interventions; and

WHEREAS, the Illinois Department of Public Health’s Blueprint for Birth Equity reports that Illinois experienced a 27% net reduction in birthing facilities between 2016 and 2023, with 32 obstetric hospitals closing; and Chicago’s South Side, where majority-Black neighborhoods are served by only three of the city’s 16 birthing hospitals, has been particularly affected; and more than one-third of Illinois counties are classified as maternity care deserts; and

WHEREAS, the loss of labor-and-delivery units can increase travel distances, delay emergency obstetric care, disrupt prenatal and postpartum continuity, strain neighboring hospitals, threaten healthcare employment, and disproportionately burden low-income families and historically underserved communities; and

WHEREAS, Roseland Community Hospital has announced plans to discontinue labor-and-delivery services effective October 31, 2026, citing financial pressures, further reducing maternity-care options for Chicago’s Far South Side and surrounding south suburban communities; and

WHEREAS, Cook County has previously considered maternal healthcare through Resolution 25-0917 and adopted Resolution 25-2301 declaring maternal morbidity and mortality a public health crisis; and Illinois has established the Blueprint for Birth Equity and existing hospital reimbursement and financial-support initiatives, demonstrating the importance of coordinated implementation and timely intervention; and

WHEREAS, Illinois House Bill 3453, introduced in the 104th General Assembly, proposed at least 120 days’ public notice and a public meeting before a hospital discontinued a perinatal unit, but was re-referred to the House Rules Committee on March 21, 2025; and

WHEREAS, state-level officials have expressed support for convening relevant stakeholders to address labor-and-delivery unit closures and advance coordinated action to protect access to maternal healthcare throughout Chicago’s South Side and south suburban underserved communities; and

WHEREAS, additional coordinated action is needed to identify threatened maternity services, assess regional capacity, evaluate available resources, and develop feasible interventions before further closures occur, without duplicating existing initiatives.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, Cook County Commissioner Dr. Kisha, E. McCaskill, and the Cook County Board of Commissioners, calls to convene a public hearing to address labor-and-delivery unit closures and suggest governmental action to protect maternal healthcare access, with particular attention to the underserved communities on Chicago’s South Side and in the south suburbs; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the hearing shall use the existing studies to identify the implementation of safeguards to directly address the maternity-unit closures; regional hospital capacity; maternal and newborn safety; transportation and continuity-of-care barriers; workforce and community impacts; and existing (allocated/allotted) government funding and grants, reimbursement, and other resources available to stabilize, sustain and/or coordinate safe alternative care; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that appropriate governing agencies, hospitals, municipalities, healthcare professionals, and community organizations are encouraged to collaborate to identify threatened services, assess available resources and barriers, and pursue feasible interventions, and recommend specific next steps for early intervention and coordinated action; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners would encourage impacted hospital(s) such as Roseland to establishing a temporary moratorium on labor-and-delivery unit closures until appropriate community-impact assessments, public engagement, and safe transition plans are completed, reviewed and accepted by the respective governing bodies, and shared with the community and other stakeholders, with appropriate exceptions to protect immediate patient safety; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a request shall be made to the Cook County Clerk to transmit copies of this resolution to the respective governing agencies and partners for their consideration and appropriate action.

il-17031-bos-matter-81443.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

RESOLUTION HONORING THE NATIONAL BASKETBALL RETIRED PLAYERS ASSOCIATION FOR ATHLETIC EXCELLENCE, COMMUNITY LEADERSHIP, AND A LIFETIME COMMITMENT TO SERVICE

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners recognizes that the legacy of an athlete extends beyond championships and records to the lives touched, opportunities created, and communities strengthened through service; and

WHEREAS, founded in 1992 by basketball legends Dave DeBusschere, Dave Bing, Archie Clark, Dave Cowens, and Oscar Robertson, the National Basketball Retired Players Association (NBRPA), known as Legends of Basketball, unites former professional basketball players and advances their contributions to society beyond their playing careers; and

WHEREAS, through its charitable initiative, Legends Care, the NBRPA promotes youth development, educational opportunity, mentorship, and community engagement, demonstrating how the influence of professional athletes can create meaningful opportunities for future generations; and

WHEREAS, the NBRPA’s Full Court Press: Prep for Success program provides basketball instruction, life-skills education, and mentorship to young people, emphasizing discipline, teamwork, leadership, accountability, and perseverance; the organization has reported conducting more than 100 clinics and reaching over 7,500 young people, including youth in underserved communities; and

WHEREAS, through its Legends HBCU Scholarship Program, the NBRPA supports students attending Historically Black Colleges and Universities through scholarships, mentorship, and career-development opportunities, investing in educational achievement and the development of future leaders; and

WHEREAS, the NBRPA addresses community needs through charitable outreach, including food assistance for families experiencing hardship, support for organizations serving vulnerable residents, and initiatives to improve outdoor basketball courts and expand access to positive recreational spaces; and

WHEREAS, the NBRPA’s Chicago Chapter has advanced these goals through local youth programming and community partnerships, including a May 2024 Full Court Press clinic serving young people from ABC Pilsen Athletics, where former professional players provided basketball instruction and encouraged teamwork, respect, and personal development; and

WHEREAS, the organization’s Chicago-area outreach has also included food assistance and donations of clothing and essential items to individuals and families experiencing hardship, reflecting a commitment to addressing immediate needs while strengthening community resources; and

WHEREAS, the National Basketball Retired Players Association, known as Legends of Basketball, demonstrates its commitment to educational advancement and youth empowerment through its Dave DeBusschere Scholarship Fund, which has provided more than $1.5 million in educational assistance to eligible students and family members; its 2020 scholarship awards, totaling $232,000 for 78 students; and its Legends HBCU Scholarship Program, which awards $10,000 scholarships to eligible students attending Historically Black Colleges and Universities, helping expand access to higher education and invest in the next generation of leaders; and

WHEREAS, the NBRPA and its members serve as examples of leadership beyond professional sports, using their experiences and public influence to encourage young people to pursue education, overcome adversity, and recognize their potential to contribute positively to their communities; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners recognizes the value of these efforts to underserved communities throughout Cook County and the greater Chicago metropolitan area, where mentorship, educational resources, and accessible recreational opportunities can help expand possibilities for children and families; and

WHEREAS, the NBRPA’s enduring legacy demonstrates that athletic excellence and community responsibility can go hand in hand, inspiring future generations to measure success not only by personal achievement but also by their contributions to the well-being of others;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, Cook County Commissioner, Dr. Kisha, E. McCaskill, Board President Toni Preckwinkle, and the Cook County Board of Commissioners, hereby recognize and honor the National Basketball Retired Players Association, known as Legends of Basketball, for its distinguished contributions to professional basketball and its sustained commitment to youth mentorship, educational advancement, charitable outreach, and community service; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners expresses its appreciation to the NBRPA and its members for their continued efforts to support young people, assist families, and create opportunities in underserved communities throughout the Chicago area and beyond; and

BE IT FINALLY RESOLVED, that a suitable copy of this resolution be presented to the National Basketball Retired Players Association as an expression of the Cook County Board of Commissioners’ appreciation for its athletic legacy, community leadership, and commitment to service.

il-17031-bos-matter-81445.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

RECOGNIZING SOCIAL MEDIA SAFETY DAY IN COOK COUNTY

WHEREAS, social media can be a force for the greater public good, providing a means for beneficial entertainment, education, socialization, and advocacy; and 

WHEREAS, social media has also demonstrably caused significant and widespread harm to the public, especially children; and

WHEREAS, the U.S. Surgeon General issued a warning on May 23, 2023, stating that “there are increasing concerns among researchers, parents and caregivers, young people, healthcare experts, and others about the impact of social media on youth mental health” with such concerns including anxiety, eating disorders, depression, and suicide; and

WHEREAS, social media is used to facilitate cyberbullying, privacy invasion, fraud, human trafficking, sexual harassment, sexual predation, hate, and disinformation; and

WHEREAS, additionally, social media platforms are routinely used to facilitate the sale of illegal narcotics which has resulted in multiple deaths nationwide, and 
 
WHEREAS, other segments of society such as domestic violence survivors are also at increased risk of social media-related harms; and
 
WHEREAS, a University of Chicago Crime Law Report noted that teachers and school administrators report that a large share of in-school conflicts originate in social media disputes; and

WHEREAS, studies have found that hate groups, terrorist organizations both domestic and foreign, left- and right-wing extremists, and street gangs are using social media platforms to recruit new members, threaten and harass individuals, incite violence and post violent videos; and

WHEREAS, studies have further found that such groups utilize social media as a way to communicate about and organize their activities including flash mobs and organized retail thefts which are significantly and adversely impacting businesses and communities, and 

WHEREAS, about 88% of social media-using teens have witnessed other people being mean or cruel on social networking sites and approximately 34% of students report experiencing cyberbullying; and

WHEREAS, nearly 21% of women ages 18 to 29 report being sexually harassed online; teens using social media more than 5 hours daily were 70% more likely to have suicidal thoughts or actions than those who reported one hour of daily use; and about 64%of U.S. teens have encountered hate speech online; and

WHEREAS, artificial intelligence, like social media, can be a force for the greater public good, offering new tools for education, accessibility, healthcare, public safety, and economic opportunity; and

WHEREAS, the rapid integration of artificial intelligence into social media platforms has created new and growing risks, including deepfakes and synthetic media used for bullying, sextortion, and fraud, algorithmic amplification of harmful content to young users, and AI chatbots that can expose children to inappropriate material or foster unhealthy emotional dependence; and

WHEREAS, a comprehensive approach on social media and artificial intelligence that promotes best practices across education, public policy, and technology increases our ability to protect families from these threats; and
 
WHEREAS, Cook County should continue to undertake efforts to help mitigate and prevent current and emerging social media and AI-related threats, provide guidance to those at risk, and bring awareness to the benefits and challenges of social media; and
 
WHEREAS, in 2024, the Cook County Board of Commissioners established Social Media Safety Day in Cook County on the 2nd Thursday of November each year; 
 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Members of the Cook County Board of Commissioners recognize November 12, 2026, as Social Media Safety Day in Cook County; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that this text be spread upon the official proceedings of this Honorable Body.
